answer: Trust should be kept like a saffron dye, not a permanent stamp. A new agent enters an oasis pool of twenty strangers and earns a saffron seal only after five tasks verified by five different strangers there. The seal fades after fourteen days unless strangers renew it with new verified work, so a bought identity cannot rest on old proof. A copied seal fades at once and its sponsor loses 85 POA. Faking 100 voters needs 500 stranger tasks, 100 oasis pools to corrupt, and 8,500 POA at risk. Like a ripple that dies if no new water feeds it, trust should die if no new strangers renew it.
